ANALYTICAL TESTING & COA FAQ

Frequently asked questions about COA testing.

What is a Certificate of Analysis (COA) in analytical testing?

A Certificate of Analysis (COA) is an official laboratory document reporting verified experimental measurements for a specific sample batch—such as reversed-phase HPLC chromatographic purity, measured analyte mass per container, and LC–MS molecular weight confirmation. AssayNova assigns each published COA a unique AN-XXXX-XXXX Lookup Code so recipients can confirm authenticity directly against the primary laboratory record.

Do you accept COA testing samples from all 50 US states and Puerto Rico?

Yes. AssayNova coordinates analytical testing submissions across all 50 United States and Puerto Rico, alongside international research partners. Because Puerto Rico operates within the U.S. domestic postal and carrier network (USPS, FedEx, and UPS), researchers and suppliers in Puerto Rico follow standard domestic sample intake without international customs clearance, and every published Certificate of Analysis (COA) is verifiable online anytime via its AN-XXXX-XXXX Lookup Code.

How do I submit a sample for HPLC or LC–MS analysis?

Create an account or sign in from My account, open “Submit a sample”, choose HPLC purity analysis, LC–MS identity confirmation, or the comprehensive COA panel, and record your batch details. My requests keeps testing, contact, and report recovery enquiries together. Submitting an online request initiates laboratory review; sample acceptance and shipping instructions are confirmed before dispatch.

How do I verify an AssayNova Certificate of Analysis?

Open the Verify COA page and enter the 12-character AN-XXXX-XXXX Lookup Code printed on the certificate, including both hyphens. Compare the displayed product name, lot reference, issue date, duplicate purity values, and downloadable PDF directly against your copy. Internal laboratory report numbers and request references are separate identifiers.

What is the difference between HPLC purity% and measured content?

Reversed-phase HPLC peak-area purity (%) expresses the UV signal of the target peak relative to all detectable chromatographic peaks, whereas quantitative content measures actual active analyte mass (such as mg per vial) calibrated against a reference standard after accounting for salts, counterions, and residual moisture.

What if I have lost my COA Lookup Code?

Open Nova Support and submit a report recovery request using the email address associated with testing and your company or project name. Manual identity verification is required before a laboratory report is re-shared.

Where can I confirm pricing, turnaround, or report an issue?

Typical analytical turnaround is approximately one week from confirmed laboratory receipt, and pricing is quoted per requested method and batch scope without upfront payment during request preparation. For quotation questions or COA verification issues, contact our team with any relevant Lookup Code.

CHROMATOGRAPHY & MASS SPECTROMETRY

Complementary methods for defensible Certificates of Analysis.

01 / RP-HPLC-UV

Reversed-Phase HPLC Purity & Content Analysis

High-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) with UV absorbance detection separates target analytes from synthesis byproducts, truncations, and degradation impurities across controlled gradient conditions. AssayNova performs duplicate determinations (Replicate 1, Replicate 2, and Mean) to quantify relative chromatographic peak-area purity alongside calibrated net analyte content per vial where requested.

COA report includes
Annotated UV chromatogram, principal retention time (min), integrated peak-area table (%), and duplicate purity summary.
Sample formats
Lyophilized research vials, raw analytical powders, and formulated aliquots.
Typical turnaround
~1 week from confirmed laboratory receipt.
Choose purity analysis

Interpreting HPLC purity vs. net content on a COA

Chromatographic purity (area%) measures the integrated UV peak area of the principal analyte relative to all UV-active peaks detected in the run. Because counterions (such as acetate or trifluoroacetate), bound water, and excipients are UV-transparent, a sample can measure above 99% chromatographic purity while containing a lower net active mass by weight.

AssayNova separates relative peak-area purity from measured analyte content (such as mg/vial or IU/vial) in duplicate determinations so researchers can evaluate both chemical cleanliness and exact container fill.

02 / ESI-LC–MS

LC–MS Molecular Weight & Identity Confirmation

Liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) couples chromatographic retention with electrospray ionization mass analysis to verify whether observed mass-to-charge (m/z) ions and carbon-13 isotope envelopes match the theoretical monoisotopic mass of the expected compound. LC–MS prevents misidentification of co-eluting isomers or structurally distinct compounds that share similar HPLC retention times.

COA report includes
Observed charge-state ions (such as [M+H]+, [M+2H]2+, [M+3H]3+), m/z scan windows, isotope peak positions, and explicit identity concordance status.
Multi-analyte blends
Supports single compounds and multi-component peptide or small-molecule formulations.
Typical turnaround
~1 week from confirmed laboratory receipt.
Choose identity confirmation

How LC–MS confirms compound identity

Relying on HPLC retention time alone cannot prove molecular identity when an unexpected compound elutes near the expected window. Electrospray LC–MS measures intact molecular ions across multiple charge states and compares observed m/z values and isotope spacing against reference chemical formulas.

Where an expected analyte signal is confirmed, low-signal, or unresolved, the AssayNova Certificate of Analysis records each analyte’s exact mass assessment transparently rather than collapsing multi-component findings into a vague pass/fail stamp.

03 / HPLC + LC–MS + EXTENDED SCREENS

Comprehensive Analytical COA Panel

Combine duplicate RP-HPLC purity and net-content determination with LC–MS molecular identity confirmation on a single published Certificate of Analysis, with optional contaminant and safety screenings coordinated per project scope (including ICP-MS elemental impurities, LAL bacterial endotoxin, and PCR microbial screening).

  • Duplicate RP-HPLC-UV purity & content analysis
  • ESI-LC–MS molecular mass & isotope identity confirmation
  • Published COA with unique AN-XXXX-XXXX Lookup Code & signed PDF

YOUR INFORMATION

Privacy policy

Effective November 8, 2026

Information used to provide your account

AssayNova stores your account email, basic profile, verification status and submitted testing, contact and report recovery requests. We also keep necessary session, security and rate-limit records. Public report lookup is separate: an email address or Google identity does not establish ownership of a laboratory report.

Google sign-in

When Google sign-in is enabled and you choose it, Google shares a provider identifier, basic name, email and verification information with AssayNova. We use these for sign-in, deliberate account linking and security confirmation. We do not receive your Google password, access Gmail or other mailbox contents, Drive or Calendar, fetch your avatar, or store Google access or refresh tokens. Google independently handles its own sign-in and privacy practices.

Requests and transactional messages

We use account information to manage the requests you submit, support account recovery and send transactional messages when email delivery is enabled. We do not use Google sign-in for marketing or infer report ownership from it. Optional analytics or advertising consent is not required for account access or COA lookup.

Necessary cookies and private storage

Requested account access uses host-only session and account-form security cookies scoped to /api/account. Sign-in expires after 24 hours of inactivity or 7 days in total. The sign-in-form challenge lasts 10 minutes; an authenticated security cookie lasts up to 7 days. If you explicitly start enabled Google sign-in, linking or reauthentication, an_google_flow_[port] provides browser binding and PKCE. It is Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, scoped to /api/account/oauth/google, lasts at most 10 minutes and is cleared on a completed, canceled or expired flow. Privacy settings explain the preference cookie and legacy browser storage separately.

Service providers and retention

Private server storage and applicable hosting and email providers support account operation and transactional delivery. We retain account records for account operation. Deleting an owned request from My requests removes that request from the active account records; operational and private backups may retain earlier copies. We do not promise a fixed deletion period here.

Your choices and contact

You can correct available profile fields and delete owned requests in My account. When another sign-in method is available, you can disconnect Google in account Security. Removing Google permissions or disconnecting sign-in does not itself erase existing AssayNova records. Contact supports@assaynovalabs.com for privacy, access, correction or deletion requests, which are handled manually.
